title: PP03 MODULE 2
description: Powerplant Module 2 (PP03 M2) practice exam covering propeller systems: Hartzell/Hamilton constant-speed and feathering propellers, governors, Alpha/Beta mode operation, propeller inspection and defects, and blade tracking/balancing.

questions.question: In the Hartzell propeller system, how is the propeller/power turbine of a PT6 engine prevented from accelerating beyond 106 percent RPM?
options: By limiting fuel supply to the engine
By mechanically locking the propeller shaft above that speed
questions.explanation: Overspeed protection on the PT6/Hartzell system works by limiting the fuel supplied to the engine, which limits the power available to drive the propeller/power turbine beyond 106% RPM.

questions.question: Constant speed, non-feathering propellers (such as Hartzell and similar designs without counterweights) increase pitch angle using:
questions.explanation: These propellers rely on governor oil pressure acting on the piston to increase blade pitch angle, rather than centrifugal twisting moment or spring force alone.

questions.question: Having reached the full-feathered position, further movement of the propeller pitch-change mechanism is prevented by:
options: The governor automatically locking the oil supply
Contact between the high angle stop ring in the base of the fixed cam and the stop lugs set in the teeth of the rotating cam
A shear pin that breaks at full feather
questions.explanation: Mechanical travel at full feather is physically stopped by the high angle stop ring (on the fixed cam) contacting the stop lugs on the rotating cam's teeth.

questions.question: What component is used to match the RPM of both propellers during cruise on a multi-engine aircraft?
options: A mechanical interconnect shaft between engines
A simple manual trim wheel only
questions.explanation: An electro-magnetic coil, as part of a propeller synchronizing (synchrophasing) system, senses and matches propeller RPM between engines during cruise.

questions.question: A cyclic variation in engine speed above and below the desired speed is characterized as:
questions.explanation: Hunting describes a propeller governor cycling the engine speed repeatedly above and below the target RPM instead of settling at a steady value.

questions.question: Aerodynamic unbalance of a propeller can largely be eliminated by:
options: Checking only the static (weight) balance of the hub
Checking blade contour and blade angle setting
questions.explanation: Aerodynamic unbalance results from inconsistencies in blade shape or angle between blades, so verifying blade contour and angle setting is the way to largely eliminate it.

questions.question: Which force operates to move the blade of a constant-speed counterweight-type propeller to the HIGH PITCH position?
options: Centrifugal force acting on the counterweights
questions.explanation: On a counterweight-type propeller, centrifugal force acting on the counterweights is what drives the blades toward high pitch, opposed by governor oil pressure which drives them toward low pitch.

questions.question: Front cone bottoming, where the apex of the front cone bottoms on the crankshaft splines before it seats on the hub, is corrected by:
options: Using a spacer of limited thickness behind the rear cone
Replacing the entire propeller hub assembly
questions.explanation: Front cone bottoming is corrected by installing a spacer (of no more than the specified maximum thickness) behind the rear cone, which adjusts the hub's seating position on the crankshaft.

questions.question: The force acting on a rotating propeller blade operating at a normal pitch angle that tends to increase the pitch angle is called:
questions.explanation: Blade aerodynamic force (the aerodynamic twisting moment generated by the airfoil shape) tends to increase (coarsen) the pitch angle of a rotating propeller blade.

questions.question: Repairs to an aluminum alloy adjustable-pitch propeller are NOT permitted on which of the following propeller blade areas?
questions.explanation: The shank area of an aluminum propeller blade is a highly stressed region where repairs are not permitted, unlike certain limited repairs allowed on the tip or blade face.

questions.question: When preparing a propeller blade for inspection, it should be cleaned with:
options: A stiff wire brush and solvent
questions.explanation: Propeller blades should be cleaned gently with mild soap and water prior to inspection, avoiding harsh solvents or abrasive methods that could damage or mask surface defects.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about why a propeller brake is designed?
options: To prevent the propeller from windmilling when it is feathered in flight
To decrease the time for the propeller to come to a complete stop after engine shutdown
To reduce the high RPM from the engine to a propeller RPM that can be maintained without exceeding the maximum propeller tip speed
questions.explanation: Reducing high engine RPM to a suitable propeller RPM is the job of the reduction gear assembly, not the propeller brake — so this statement is the one that is NOT true about a propeller brake's purpose.

questions.question: Why is the pulley stop screw on a propeller governor adjustable?
options: To limit the maximum propeller pitch for takeoff
To limit the maximum propeller speed during takeoff
To maintain the proper blade angle for cruising
questions.explanation: The pulley stop screw is adjustable so that the maximum propeller speed during takeoff can be set and limited to the correct value.

questions.question: When operating in flight (Alpha) mode, as the power lever is moved forward while the propeller governor operates in its constant-speed mode:
options: Only fuel flow increases, with no change in horsepower
Both fuel flow and engine horsepower increase
Only propeller RPM increases, with fuel flow unchanged
questions.explanation: Moving the power lever forward in Alpha mode increases both fuel flow and the resulting engine horsepower, while the governor holds propeller RPM constant by adjusting blade angle.

questions.question: The process of determining the position of the tips of the propeller blades relative to each other is called:
questions.explanation: Blade tracking is specifically the process of checking that all propeller blade tips follow the same plane of rotation relative to one another.

questions.question: Shallow, thin lines or marks varying in degree of depth and width on a propeller surface are called:
questions.explanation: Scratches are defined as shallow, thin surface lines or marks of varying depth and width, as distinguished from deeper, more localized defects like nicks or gouges.

questions.question: The Propeller Control Lever is used to:
options: Control blade angle directly in the Beta mode only
Control system RPM in the Alpha mode
Shut off fuel to the engine
questions.explanation: The Propeller Control Lever (condition lever) controls the target system RPM when the propeller is operating in the Alpha (flight) mode.

questions.question: When accumulator unfeathering is used, the accumulator's purpose is to:
options: Provide oil pressure to the governor and then to the propeller
Provide electrical power to the feathering pump motor
Store fuel for an emergency restart
questions.explanation: An unfeathering accumulator stores pressurized oil, which is released to supply oil pressure first to the governor and then on to the propeller to unfeather the blades.

questions.question: Applicable instructions for a propeller that remains installed and stored on the aircraft are found in the:
questions.explanation: Storage and preservation instructions for a propeller that stays installed on the aircraft are found in the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM).

questions.question: When the engine is operating at exactly the RPM called for by the pilot, the governor closes the passage between the engine and the propeller. This:
options: Causes the propeller to immediately feather
Forces maximum oil flow to the propeller continuously
Prevents oil from going to or draining from the propeller
questions.explanation: At the exact selected (on-speed) RPM, the governor closes off the oil passage, holding the propeller's current blade angle by preventing oil from flowing to or draining from the propeller.

questions.question: When inspecting wooden blades on a ground-adjustable propeller, special attention needs to be given to the:
questions.explanation: The shank area of a wooden ground-adjustable propeller blade requires special inspection attention due to the high stress concentration in that region.

questions.question: On a propeller operating in Beta mode, blade angle is controlled by the:
questions.explanation: In Beta mode, the power lever directly controls propeller blade angle (rather than the governor controlling it in constant-speed mode, as in Alpha mode).

questions.question: When engine power is increased on a counterweight-type propeller governor system, what is the resulting action on blade angle?
options: Blade angle remains fixed regardless of power change
Blade angle decreases to maintain the selected RPM
Blade angle increases to maintain the selected RPM
questions.explanation: As power (and the resulting twisting moment) increases, the governor increases blade angle (coarsens pitch) to absorb the added power while holding the selected RPM constant.

questions.question: During Alpha operation, when the power lever is moved to the aft position on a propeller using a CSU (Constant Speed Unit), the blade angle will:
questions.explanation: Moving the power lever aft during Alpha operation reduces power demand, and the CSU responds by decreasing blade angle to maintain the selected RPM at the lower power setting.

questions.question: What type of oil is used for servicing a hydromatic propeller, when necessary?
questions.explanation: Hydromatic propellers are serviced using engine oil, matching the oil already circulating in the engine's own lubrication system, rather than a separate dedicated fluid.

questions.question: During inspection of wood propellers, which of the following defects is a possible cause for rejection?
options: No protective coating on the propeller
Solder missing from screw heads securing metal tipping
An oversize hub or bolt hole, or elongated bolt holes
questions.explanation: An oversize or elongated bolt/hub hole compromises the structural fit and fastening of the propeller, making it a cause for rejection, unlike the other listed (less severe) findings.

questions.question: What type of defect is detected during inspection of a propeller blade by dye penetrant inspection?
questions.explanation: Dye penetrant inspection is specifically used to reveal surface-breaking defects such as cracks, which would not otherwise be visible to the naked eye.

questions.question: What must be done to avoid confusing the sounds of a tapping (coin-tap) test on a composite propeller blade and cuff area?
options: Coin tap the cuff area and the blade area simultaneously until a sound difference is recognized
Coin tap the leading edge guard area and the cuff transition area with different tapping coins
Coin tap the cuff area and the transition area between the cuff and the blade separately from the blade area
questions.explanation: Because the cuff/transition area and the blade area can produce naturally different tap sounds due to their different construction, they should be coin-tapped separately to avoid misinterpreting a normal difference as a defect.

questions.question: What is the out-of-track limit of a metal propeller?
questions.explanation: The standard out-of-track limit for a metal propeller blade is 1/16 inch, beyond which the propeller must be adjusted or repaired before further flight.

questions.question: In a constant-speed feathering propeller, if the governor-supplied oil is lost during operation, what will happen to the pitch angle of the propeller blades?
options: Pitch angle decreases and the propeller un-feathers
Pitch angle and RPM both decrease together
Pitch angle increases and the propeller feathers
questions.explanation: Loss of governor oil removes the force holding the blades at a lower pitch, so counterweights/springs (or air loads, depending on design) drive the blades toward high pitch, feathering the propeller as a fail-safe.

questions.question: What is the function of the reduction gear assembly in turboprop aircraft?
options: Reduce the high RPM from the engine to a propeller RPM that can be efficiently used
Reduce the power of the engine to maintain a constant RPM
Increase the propeller thrust during takeoff directly
questions.explanation: The reduction gear assembly steps down the engine's (gas generator/power turbine) high RPM to a lower RPM suitable for efficient propeller operation.

questions.question: How is oil from the governor of a Hartzell constant-speed feathering propeller supplied to the hydraulic piston?
options: Through an external pipe line routed to the propeller hub
Through a lubricating fitting on the hub
questions.explanation: Governor oil is routed to the propeller's hydraulic piston through a hollow passage in the engine's propeller shaft, rather than through external hub fittings or piping.

questions.question: What is the approximate allowable depth of a repaired edge defect on a propeller blade?
questions.explanation: A repaired edge defect on a propeller blade is generally limited to an approximate maximum depth of 1/8 inch, within the manufacturer's repair limits.

questions.question: Among the unfeathering methods implemented in light aircraft, which one is used in light training aircraft?
questions.explanation: Light training aircraft commonly use air-oil accumulator pressure as a simple, self-contained method to unfeather the propeller after an in-flight feathering demonstration.

questions.question: What action takes place when the cockpit control lever for a hydromatic constant-speed propeller is actuated?
options: The governor booster pump oil is supplied directly to the feathering pump
Compression of the governor speeder spring is changed
The governor relief valve starts to bypass the governor boosted oil
questions.explanation: Moving the cockpit (RPM/pitch) control lever changes the compression of the governor's speeder spring, which resets the target (selected) RPM the governor will maintain.

questions.question: What prevents the propeller from going into reverse or below the primary blade angle in the event of a beta system malfunction in flight?
questions.explanation: The lock-pitch solenoid valve is specifically designed to prevent the blades from moving into reverse or below the primary (flight idle) blade angle if the beta control system malfunctions in flight.

questions.question: In the Hamilton Standard hydromatic propeller, which assembly contains both the blades and the mechanical means for holding them in position?
questions.explanation: The propeller hub assembly houses the blades themselves along with the mechanical retention (bearing and clamping) components that hold them in position.

questions.question: How is feathering accomplished in Hartzell counterweighted feathering propellers?
options: By releasing the governor oil pressure, allowing the counterweights and feathering spring to feather the blades
By supplying governor oil pressure, allowing the counterweights and feathering spring to feather the blades
By supplying engine pump oil pressure to assist the feathering spring against the counterweight force
questions.explanation: Feathering is achieved by releasing (venting) the governor oil pressure that normally holds the blades at a lower pitch, letting the counterweights and feathering spring drive the blades to the feathered position.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT considered a cause of rejection for wooden propellers?
options: A crack or deep cut across the grain
questions.explanation: Minor surface scratches are generally not, by themselves, a cause for rejection, unlike more serious structural defects such as cracks across the grain or empty/damaged screw and bolt holes.

questions.question: The hydraulic cylinder of a Hartzell propeller, which provides power for changing pitch, is mounted on:
options: Inside the hub, with no external mounting
questions.explanation: On Hartzell propellers, the pitch-change hydraulic cylinder is mounted on the front of the propeller hub.

questions.question: An increase in oil pressure in the PT6 Hartzell propeller system drives the blades towards:
questions.explanation: On the PT6/Hartzell system, increasing governor oil pressure drives the blades toward low pitch, opposing the counterweights/springs that otherwise drive the blades toward high pitch/feather.

questions.question: What force in the hydromatic propeller (R1830) takes the propeller blade angle into high pitch?
questions.explanation: In the R1830 hydromatic propeller, governor-boosted oil is the force that drives the blade angle toward high pitch.

questions.question: During normal in-flight unfeathering, what will happen if the propeller condition lever is positioned into the normal flight range?
options: It causes the governor to connect the propeller oil supply to the drain
It causes the governor to connect the governed oil to the drain
It reconnects the governed oil to the supply line from the governor
questions.explanation: Moving the condition lever back into the normal flight range reconnects governed oil from the governor to the propeller supply line, restoring normal constant-speed control as part of the unfeathering sequence.

questions.question: Constant speed, non-feathering propellers such as Hartzell and others with similar design, without counterweights, increase pitch angle using:
questions.explanation: As with the earlier item on this same topic, these propeller designs rely on governor oil pressure (rather than counterweights) to increase blade pitch angle.

questions.question: When does the distributor valve of the hydromatic propeller shift?
questions.explanation: The distributor valve shifts specifically during the un-feathering sequence, redirecting oil flow appropriately to bring the blades out of the feathered position.

questions.question: Centrifugal force acting on the blade counterweights of most Hartzell aluminum and steel hub propeller models is used to:
questions.explanation: On these Hartzell models, centrifugal force on the counterweights works to increase (coarsen) blade pitch, opposing the governor oil pressure that decreases pitch.

questions.question: What is the status of the propeller governor during the beta mode of operation?
questions.explanation: During beta mode, the governor operates in an under-speed condition, since blade angle (not the governor) is directly controlling propeller behavior via the power lever at this stage.

questions.question: During beta operation of turboprop propellers, what is the mode of operation of the propeller governor?
questions.explanation: As with the previous item, the propeller governor remains in an under-speed condition during beta operation, consistent with direct power-lever control of blade angle in this mode.

questions.question: What prevents the feathering spring and counterweights from feathering the propeller when the engine is shut down (on the ground)?
questions.explanation: Automatically removable high pitch stops engage to prevent the feathering spring and counterweights from driving the propeller fully into feather during normal ground shutdown.

questions.question: Which lever is used for RPM control in Alpha mode?
questions.explanation: RPM in Alpha (flight) mode is controlled using the propeller lever, which sets the target RPM that the governor then maintains.

questions.question: What is the definition of propeller (blade) tracking?
options: The process of determining the positions of the tips of the propeller blades relative to each other
The process of adjusting blade pitch to match engine RPM
The process of determining the static balance of the propeller assembly
questions.explanation: Blade tracking specifically refers to checking and comparing the relative tip positions of all propeller blades to ensure they rotate in the same plane.

questions.question: What is the out-of-track limit for a metal propeller?
questions.explanation: As with the earlier item on this topic, the standard out-of-track limit for a metal propeller is 1/16 inch.

questions.question: In the Hartzell propeller system, how is the propeller prevented from accelerating beyond 106% RPM?
options: By automatically reducing propeller blade angle to zero
By a mechanical overspeed brake on the propeller shaft
questions.explanation: As covered earlier, overspeed protection works by limiting fuel supply to the engine, which limits available power rather than mechanically braking the propeller.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the arbor used in propeller balancing?
options: To support the propeller on a knife edge (or similar low-friction support) for balancing
To measure the propeller's moment of inertia
To apply torque during propeller installation
questions.explanation: A balancing arbor supports the propeller hub on knife edges (or rollers) with minimal friction, allowing any heavy point to rotate the assembly downward and reveal unbalance.

questions.question: Horizontal unbalance in a wooden propeller is typically corrected by:
options: Trimming material from the tip only
Adding or removing washers under the hub bolts
questions.explanation: Horizontal (chordwise) unbalance in a wooden propeller is commonly corrected by adding a solder piece at the appropriate location to balance the blade.

questions.question: What is good practice for storing a wood propeller?
options: Leaned at a steep angle against a wall
questions.explanation: Wood propellers should be stored in a horizontal position to avoid uneven moisture absorption and warping that can occur with vertical storage.

questions.question: What tool is used to dress out minor surface damage on a propeller blade?
options: Coarse sandpaper alone, with no file
questions.explanation: A spoon-shaped riffle file is specifically shaped to dress out and blend minor surface damage (nicks, scratches) on the curved surface of a propeller blade.
